segments.t: And I just was, I forget, I guess I'm dating myself.
I forget that so many people haven't lived this,
but what were you doing in 1999?
How were you in 1999?
In 1999, I was just graduating from college.
I was writing about mergers and acquisitions,
the height of the boom in the M&A business
for the New York Times, that's what I was doing.
And this was a heck of a time.
So anyway, we are literally exactly like 1999
in the sense that we have kind of a two-speed economy.
But does that mean to you again,
I remember you saying this idea
that the market still has 40% to run.
Does that mean that in terms of this thing cresting,
we are still years away or we're still months away
and then therefore, how do you trade that?
So I think that for me, the most interesting thing,
and it's hard for me to see professionally
much beyond December 31
because that's gonna be really important obviously for a fund.
So I'm trying to tactically think
what I wanna do for the rest of the year.
Clearly, if you kind of just go back
and look at midterm cycles, a whole variety of things,
it would tell you that we should have
a really, really strong fourth quarter
coming out of the midterms.
The market typically bottom sometime,
late October, early November,
and then you get the fourth quarter push.
I kind of look at positioning and think that's very possible.
At the same time, if I was thinking for a year from now,
2027 is gonna be really, really challenging
for the stock market.
And I say that because if I just look at the flows
and that's probably what we look at the most,
it's what I look at the most, you've probably got...
